title: 5 Dollars (Federal Reserve Note; colored)

issuing_entity.name: United States Department of the Treasury

obverse.description:
Portrait of Abraham Lincoln at center.
Treasurer's signature and Federal Reserve Seal at left.
Secretary's signature and Treasury Seal to right.
Great Seal of the United States in background to right.
obverse.lettering:
FEDERAL RESERVE NOTE
THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
THIS NOTE IS LEGAL TENDER
FOR ALL DEBTS, PUBLIC AND PRIVATE
FIVE DOLLARS

reverse.lettering:
THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
IN GOD WE TRUST

LINCOLN MEMORIAL
FIVE DOLLARS

comments:
Issued by the Federal Reserve and was unveiled to the American public on September 20, 2007 and was issued into general circulation on March 13, 2008. This note is part of the NextGen series produced by the Bureau of Engraving and Printing and issued through the Federal Reserve System. Each of the five denominations feature Symbols of Freedom, for the $5 Federal Reserve Note, it features the Great Seal of the United States. Although not included when the current series of notes was introduced, this denomination was included as a response to reports that counterfeiters were bleaching $5 Federal Reserve Notes and used the genuine paper to produce counterfeit $100 Federal Reserve Notes.

Note: Code Letters of the Federal Reserve Branches

* A/1 - Boston, Massachusetts
* B/2 - New York, New York
* C/3 - Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
* D/4 - Cleveland, Ohio
* E/5 - Richmond, Virginia
* F/6 - Atlanta, Georgia
* G/7 - Chicago, Illinois
* H/8 - St. Louis, Missouri
* I/9 - Minneapolis, Minnesota
* J/10 - Kansas City, Missouri
* K/11 - Dallas, Texas
* L/12 - San Francisco, California

 

The Fort Worth (FW) mark is located by the front plate number at the lower right.
Replacement notes are indicated by the presence of a star (✩) at the end of their serial number.
